versions.changelog: Test GPU button (Settings, Speed and storage): short 1080p H.264 and 4K HEVC 10-bit test transcodes through each path (full GPU, GPU encode only, CPU) with speed and errors. Activity page: Cancel running transcodes and Retry or Redo finished ones.

Cleaner settings page: tabs for Profiles, Devices, Speed and storage, and Advanced; profiles are compact cards with a summary and a size-per-hour estimate; simple choices for resolution, video format and audio; the GPU section shows what Jellyfin is set to. Activity page: summary tiles, an encoder badge, and collapsible error details.

Full GPU pipeline for Intel and AMD (QSV or VAAPI on Linux): decoding, scaling and HDR tone mapping now also run on the GPU. Falls back to GPU encode only, then CPU, per file. Can be turned off in the settings.

Encode on the GPU using Jellyfin's own hardware acceleration settings (NVENC, Quick Sync, VAAPI, VideoToolbox, AMF, RKMPP), with automatic CPU fallback if the GPU encode fails. The activity page shows which encoder each transcode used.

New "Download Transcodes" dashboard page: live progress (percent, speed, time left) for running transcodes, a history of past ones with size savings and errors, and the cached copies with a delete button.

Fix "Download incomplete" in the Jellyfin Android app: apps that resume downloads now get "retry later" while the smaller copy is prepared instead of a live stream without a size. Default for items not yet transcoded is now "prepare in background". Falls back to the original if transcoding fails.

name: Download Transcoder
description: When an app downloads a video for offline use (for example the download button in the Jellyfin Android app), this plugin sends a transcoded MP4 at a resolution and bitrate chosen per device type (phone, tablet, TV, computer) instead of the original file. Uses Jellyfin's own ffmpeg, caches results and can pre-transcode new items.
overview: Serve smaller, transcoded files when clients download media
